faq_blocks_without_answer_marker.question: Q2. Who can file an RTI request? A: Any person can file an RTI request - citizens, businesses, NGOs, and even non citizens. There is no age restriction ( though minors typically require guardian assistance ).

faq_blocks_without_answer_marker.section: L.l What is RTI & Basic Rights
faq_blocks_without_answer_marker.question: Q3. Is RTI available in Chhattisgarh? A: Yes, completely. Chhattisgarh State Information Commission (SIC) is operational at Naya Raipur and handles all RTI matters at state level. All state departments must comply.

faq_blocks_without_answer_marker.section: L.l What is RTI & Basic Rights
faq_blocks_without_answer_marker.question: Q4. Do I need to give a reason for requesting information? A: No. You can request any information without giving any reason or justification. Section 6(2) explicitly states you don't need to provide reasons.

faq_blocks_without_answer_marker.question: Q20. Can [ request information in Hindi? A: Yes, you can file RTI in English, Hindi, or any official language of the area. PIO must respond in the same language or English.
Q21. How long does it take to get RTI response in Chhattisgarh? A: Standard: 30 days from receipt of application. Emergency (life liberty cases): 48 hours
Q22. If no response is received within 30 days, what happens? A: The application is "deemed refused" you can immediately appeal without waiting for formal rejection letter.
Q23. Can the 3O day deadline be extended? A: Yes if third party notification is required (Section ll ) , the deadline extends to 40 days.
Q24. What if 1 don't receive response within 30 days? A: You can file First Appeal within 30 days of the deemed refusal to a senior officer.
Q25. Will [ get response on the exact 3Oth day? A: No, deadline is "within 30 days" meaning by the end of 3Oth Response can come any up to day 30. day. day
Q26. How much is the RTI application fee in Chhattisgarh? A: 3l0 per application (onetime fee)
Q27. Are there additional charges if I want printed copies? A: Yes, copy charge is =2 per page for black & white printouts.
Q28. What if 1 want information in digital format ( CD, email)? A: You may pay cost of medium (CDIDVD) typically 310 20. Email delivery is usually free.
Q29. Are BPL persons required to pay RTI fees? A: No, completely exempt. Just provide BPL certificate copy with application
Q31. What if I cannot afford the fee? A: File application stating economic hardship. PIO may waive fees if satisfied.
Q32. If PIO doesn t respond within 30 days, do I get free information? A: Yes! Per Section 7(6), if PIO fails to meet deadline, information is provided free of charge.
Q33. Can fees be refunded if application is rejected? A: No, application fee is non- refundable even if request is rejected.
Q34. Are there fees for First Appeal or Second Appeal? A: No appeals to SIC senior officer are free. No fee charged.
Q35. What is the maximum fee I can be charged? A: For =2 per page standard rate. Actual cost if higher No arbitrary charges allowed. copies:
Q36. What is a Public Information Officer ( PIO)? A: The designated official in each department responsible for receiving and processing RTI applications per Section 5.
Q37. How do I find the PIO of a department? A: Check the departments website name, email, phone), ask at department office, or call Suchna Aayog helpline.

Q38. Can [ file RTI with Assistant PIO instead of main PIO? A: Yes, Assistant PIO (at sub- divisional level) can accept applications. Response timeline increases by 5 days if filed with Assistant PIO.
Q39. What if PIO doesn't respond? A: Per Section 7(2), this is "deemed refusal" and you can appeal immediately
Q40. Can I ask who the PIO is? A: Tes, every department must publish PIO's name and contact details. You can request this information itself.
Q41. Can I ask for information that doesn't exist yet? A: you can only request information that already exists If it doesn't exist, PIO must reject stating reason. No,
Q42. Can I request analysis or reports not already prepared? A: you cannot ask PIO to create new reports. You can only request already existing documents. No,

Q43. Can [ request information about a specific person? A: Only if it's related to public activity or government function. Personal information unrelated to public activity is protected ( Section 8(1) (j)).
Q44. Can [ ask for copies of government contracts? A: Yes, government contracts are public information. You can request copies of contracts between government and vendors.

Q45. Can I request salary details of government employees? A: Yes, salary information of all government officers is public ( Section 4 requires this publication) . But personal details oflower staff may be protected.
Q46. Can I ask about budget allocation? A: Yes, budget allocations are public information. Every department must publish budget details (Section 4(1) (b) (xi)).
Q47. Can I request information about government meetings? A: Yes, you can request minutes of meetings, decisions taken, but not internal deliberations ( those are Cabinet papers).
Q48. Can I ask for details about government tenders? A: Yes, all tender documents, criteria, and award details are public. Sealed bids of other companies are confidential until opening.
Q49. Can I request list of beneficiaries of government scheme? A: you can request complete list of who received benefits under any government program. Yes,
Q50. Can Iask for copies of FIRs ( Police complaints)? A: Partially yes you can get details if you're a victim stakeholder Investigation details may be withheld (Section 8(1) (h)).
Q52. Can I get information about national security? A: No, national security is exempt (Section 8(l) (a) ). But public interest can override in some cases.
Q53. Can [ request information about Cabinet discussions? A: internal Cabinet deliberations are protected ( Section 8(1) (i)). But final Cabinet decisions must be disclosed. No,
Q54. What if I want competitor information? A: Commercial confidentiality ( trade secrets) cannot be disclosed ( Section 8(a)(d) ) unless public interest is strong
Q55. Can I get medical records of patients? A: medical information is personal and private (Section 8(1) (j)) unless public health emergency. No,
Q56. Can I request sealed tender bids of other companies? A: No, sealed bids are confidential ( Section 8(1) (d)). After bid opening winners bid becomes public.
Q57. Are government employee personal details protected? A: Personal details (address, phone, family info) are protected. But official designation, salary performance is public.
Q58. Can government refuse information claiming efficiency harm? A: No, "efficiency" is not valid exemption. Only specific exemptions in Section 8 apply.
Q59. Can Ibe denied information because it's "sensitive"? A: "sensitive" alone is not valid exemption. Must fall under specific Section 8 categories. No,

Q60. What is Section 8(2) -Public Interest Override? A: Even exempt information can be disclosed if public interest in disclosure outweighs harm. Example: Corruption evidence overrides commercial confidentiality.
Q61. What is thirdrparty information? A: Information relating to another person (company, individual) provided to government in confidence.
Q62. How is third party information handled? A: PIO notifies third party within 5 gives them 10 days to object, then decides within 40 days ( not 30). days,
Q63. Can I get information about another person's RTI request? A: No, that person's information is confidential ( third party confidentiality).
Q64. Can I request tender details of competing companies? A: Preraward: NO (confidential). Post award: YES for winning company details.
Q65. What happens if third party objects to disclosure? A: PIO considers objection, applies public interest test. Objection is not automatic reason for denial.
Q66. How long does third party notification add to timeline? A: 1O additional days (third party 10 days to respond) . Total: 40 days instead of 30. gets
Q67. Can third party appeal against disclosure? A: Yes, third party can file appeal to State Information Commission against disclosure decision.
Q68. Is employee information considered "third party"? A: Partially. Public information (salary, designation ) isn't third party. Personal details (address family) are.
Q69. Can I get details about another person's contract? A: Government's side yes (contract terms, vendor details). Vendor's proprietary details may be withheld.
Q70. What if third party is a competitor bidder? A: Their sealed bid is protected. After award, winning bidder's accepted terms are public (but cost may be protected if commercial).
Q71. Can I ask for information in specific format? A: Yes, you can request printed, email, CD,or inspection. PIO should provide requested format unless resource intensive.
Q72. Can I ask to inspect records instead of getting copies? A: Tes, you have right to inspect ( Section 2(j)) this is often free and faster
Q73. Can information be provided via email? A: Tes, if applicant provides email address and PIO can digitize. Email is usually free.
Q74. What if requested format is not available? A: PIO can provide alternate format but must inform you and charge accordingly.
Q75. Can I ask for soft copies instead of printed copies? A: Yes, this reduces cost ( =2 page for vs. few rupees for CDlemail). print
Q76. Is there charge for inspection without copying? A: No, inspection is usually free. You only pay if you want copies.
Q77. Can I photograph documents during inspection? A: Personal copies during inspection are not charged (Section 7(5)).
Q78. How do 1 get information if Tm illiterate? A: PIO must provide reasonable assistance (Section 7(4 )). Can provide audio, oral, or translated version.
Q79. Can I ask for translated information? A: Yes, if you need Hindi English translation. Reasonable translation assistance must be provided.
Q80. What if document is in poor condition? A: PIO will provide best available copy. If not reproducible, must inform and may deny copy (but must allow inspection). they
Q81. Can [ request information about myself? A: Yes, you can always personal information held by government (if not restricted by other laws). get
Q82. What is "life and liberty" exception? A: Information concerning someone's lifel physical safety is urgent must be provided within 48 hours (not 30 days).
Q83. Can I request information about ongoing court case? A: Limited yes - you can request government documents filed in court. Internal investigation details may be withheld.
Q84. Can I get information during emergency? A: Yes, life liberty information 48hour deadline. Other emergencies don't have special timeline. gets
Q85. Can [ request information about police cases? A: You can request FIR details, charge sheet if you're stakeholder Investigation techniques sources are protected (Section 8(1 ) (h)).
Q86. Can I get information about election? A: Tes, election data is public. But candidate personal details and voting patterns are confidential.
Q87. Can I request information about propertylland? A: Yes, land records, property tax, ownership details are public information.
Q88. Can [ get old historical documents? A: Yes, documents 20+ years old are automatically disclosed ( Section 8(3) ) except sovereigntyllegislative privilege cabinet papers.
Q89. Can government say "file will be searched" and delay? A: No, if information exists, PIO must provide within 30 days. "File not found" is not valid excuse.
Q90. Can I request information about deceased person? A: Tes, public information about deceased officials is available. Personal details may still be protected for family

Q91. What is difference between "shall" and "may" in RTI Act? A: "Shall" = mandatory (must do). "May" = discretionary (can choose). Section 4( 2) says "shall be constant endeavor" (mandatory suo motu).
Q92. How is "reasonable time " defined for computerization? A: Not specifically defined courts interpret based on departmentis capacity. Generally 2 3 years is reasonable.
Q93. What is "disproportionate diversion of resources"? A: PIO can refuse if responding would excessively strain resources. But threshold is high must be proven.
Q94. Can PIO charge for "search and retrieval"? A: No, PIO cannot charge for finding and preparing information. Only copy costs can be charged.
Q95. Is RTI fee an application fee or information fee? A: Application fee only. You pay 310 to register request. Copy charges are separate.
Q96. What is "prescribed fee" vs "actual cost"? A: Prescribed fee is per regulation (=2 page). If actual cost is higher, PIO must justify charging more.
Q97. Can PIO refuse if applicant is serial RTI filer? A: frequency of applications doesnt matter Each application must be processed on merit. NO,
Q98. What is burden on government vs public interest? A: Section 8(2) test: Does benefit t0 public outweigh harm? Burden is not consideration -only exempt interests matter
Q102. Can PIO demand "why" for information? A: No, Section 6(2) explicitly says reason is NOT required. Asking why is violation.
Q103. Can PIO refuse application because "not in prescribed format"? A: any format (plain letter, email, portal) is acceptable. Cannot demand specific format. NO,
Q106. What if multiple people request same information? A: PIO must process each separately and within 3O-day deadline for each. Cannot batch process to save time.
Q107. Can PIO delay saying "awaiting superior approval"? A: PIO has 30 Getting internal approval must happen within this time. days. NO,
Q108. Is there deadline for PIO to even register application? A: No explicit deadline but application is deemed received on receipt date ( for timeline calculation).
Q109. What if PIO transfers application to another department? A: Original timeline pauses, receiving department gets new 30 days. You should be informed within 5 Of transfer. days
Q110. Can PIO demand applicant's identity? A: No, you only need to provide contact details. Full identity personal verification cannot be demanded.
Q112. Can "official secrets" always be withheld? A: No, Section 8(2) allows disclosure if public interest outweighs official secrecy. RTI supersedes Official Secrets Act, 1923.
Q113. What is difference between "Cabinet papers" and "government decision"? A: Cabinet papers = deliberations protected) . Government decision = outcome ( must be disclosed with reasons .
Q114. Can trade secret protection last forever? A: No, after 20 years, information becomes accessible ( Section 8(3) ) unless sovereignty cabinet papers.
Q115. What if information is both personal AND public interest? A: Balance is applied. Public interest (corruption, illegality health safety) usually overrides personal privacy.
Q116. Can "preliminary assessment" stage be withheld? A: Not as blanket exemption. Investigation details can be withheld under Section 8(1) (h), not preliminary stage alone.
Q117. What is "larger public interest" test? A: Applies to Sections 8(1)(d), (e), (j). Disclosure must serve substantial public purpose, not mere curiosity.
Q118. Can live investigation details be withheld? A: Yes, Section 8(1) (h) applies. But once case is closed, information becomes accessible.
Q119. What information about ongoing litigation must be disclosed? A: Governments position papers, affidavits filed in court, factual details must be disclosed. Legal strategy may be protected.
Q120. Can "pending decision" be withheld as "draft"? A: No, pending decisions at final stage must be disclosed. Only internal draft (pre finalization) can be withheld.
Q121. What is suo motu disclosure obligation? A: Section 4(2) - Every department must proactively publish information regularly, not wait for RTI requests
Q122. What information must be published suo motu? A: Everything listed in Section 4(1)(b) 17 categories structure, budgets, contracts, beneficiaries, procedures, etc.
Q123. Does suo motu disclosure reduce RTI applications? A: Yes, and that's the goal. If information is already published, RTI process is faster
Q124. What is timeline for suo motu disclosure? A: Within 120 days of RTI Act enactment (already passed), then ongoing annual updates required.
Q125. Can department fail suo motu disclosure? A: Yes, many departments are noncompliant. You can complain to SIC about inadequate suo motu disclosure.
Q126. What if requested information is already published? A: PIO should provide reference link. Cannot charge copy fee if already publicly available.
Q127. How is suo motu disclosure monitored? A: State Information Commission prepares annual report on compliance. Citizens can also file complaints
Q128. Can departments choose what to disclose suo motu? A: Section 4(1)(b) mandates 17 specific categories. Departments cannot selectively disclose. NO,
Q129. Is department website updating considered suo motu disclosure? A: Partially yes, but Section 4 requires specific 17 items to be published within prescribed format.
Q130. What if department's website information is incomplete? A: You can file RTI for missing information, or complaint to SIC about non compliance with Section 4.
Q131. What can State Information Commission do? A: Pass binding orders on PIOs, recommend penalties (up to =25,OOO) , award compensation, initiate suo motu investigations.
Q132. Can SIC order compensation for delay ? Aः Yes, SIC can award compensation if delay caused hardship. Amount is discretionary ( =5OO 5,OOO typical).
Q133. Can SIC penalize PIO for slow response? A: Tes, can recommend penalties for repeated violations (up to 325,OO0) or disciplinary action including dismissal.
Q134. What if SIC order is not complied? A: You can file contempt petition in High Court against non compliance.
Q135. Can SIC modify PIO's decision? A: Yes, in appeal, SIC can order disclosure of previously withheld information if it disagrees with exemption claim.
Q136. Can SIC conduct suo motu investigation? A: Yes, SIC can take up suo motu cases based on media reports or public knowledge about RTI violations.
Q137. What is "larger public interest" per SIC interpretation? A: Varies by case, but generally includes corruption exposure, health safety risks constitutional violations environmental threats.
Q138. How long does SIC take to decide? A: 90 days from appeal receipt (extendable by 90 more days for complex cases).
Q139. Can SIC recommend criminal action? A: Tes, SIC can recommend police prosecution for willful violations Section 23 penalties).
Q140. Can SIC order interim relief? A: Yes, SIC can pass interim orders directing immediate disclosure while case is ongoing.
Q141. What if PIO says "file is with another department, we'll get it after 15 days"? A: PIO still has 3O day obligation. Internal delays are not excuse. You should escalate if deadline isnt met.
Q142. Can PIO extend 3O day deadline by claiming "voluminous information"? A: voluminous data is not valid reason per Section 7. PIO must manage within 30 days. No,
Q143. If 1 file RTIon 3Oth of month, when is deadline - 29th or 3Oth? A: Deadline is 30 days from receipt. If received on 3Oth, deadline is 3Oth of next month (or last day of month if shorter ).
Q144. What if received on 3lst, how is 30 days counted? A: From 3lst, counting 30 you to 3Oth of next month (or last day if shorter month). days gets
Q145. Does holiday affect the 3O day counting? A: No, 30 days means calendar including weekends holidays days,
Q146. Can PIO claim "we have to check 1O0 files for one piece of data"? A: No, compilation time is included in 3O-day deadline. Cannot demand extension for compilation.
Q1477. What if transfer happens on day 291 A: Receiving department full 30 days from transfer date, not remaining 1 gets day.
Q148. If third party objects late ( day 15 instead of day 1O), what happens? A: Depends if genuinely late (beyond 10), PIO may not consider. Or may extension if for good cause. day grant
Q149. Can multiple extensions make it 6O 90 days total? A: No, standard timeline is 30 days (or 40 with third party). Extensions only for specific circumstances.
Q150. If PIO is on leave, does timeline pause? A: No, timeline continues. Department must arrange another PIO or senior officer to handle during leave.
Q151. Can I demand PIO to "verify" if information exists? A: you describe what you want. PIO searches. If doesnt exist, PIO says SO with reasons. No,
Q152. Can I ask PIO to "create analysis" of existing data? A: you cannot ask for analysis. Tou can only request existing reports documents. No,
Q153. What if information exists but in unorganized form? A: PIO still must provide organized response within 30 days. Cannot claim "too scattered "
Q154. Can I ask for "all communications" between two people? A: Too vague. You must specify: emails, letters, meetings or which specific period project.
Q155. If data is partly digital and partly paper, can cost be charged for compilation? A: compilation and search is free. Only copy cost ( =2l page) can be charged. No,
Q156. Can I ask for information from before RTI Act came ( pre zOOS)? A: Yes, historical records are accessible. After 20 years ( 2025 for pre zoO5) , automatically accessible.
Q1577. What if record is damaged and partially illegible? A: PIO must provide available legible portions and inform about damage.
Q158. Can [ ask "what information does PIO have about X subject"? A: Too vague. You must be specific documents, reports, correspondence, etc.
Q159. If computer system has partial data for period, must full period be searched? Aः Yes, PIO must search all systems ( digital and paper). Cannot give partial just because some data is missing
Q160. Can [ ask "provide proof that decision was made transparently"? A: Too vague. Ask specifically: "minutes of meeting " "file noting " "approval email," etc.
Q161. 1 don't know which department has information can [ ask multiple? A: Better to file to likely department. If wrong, they transfer (5 days). Alternatively, file to Chief Secretary who can route.
Q162. If information is jointly held by 2 departments, where do [ file? A: File to primary coordinating department. They coordinate with other department within their 30day period.
Q163. What if PIO doesnt know whether they have information? A: PIO must search their records. If still not found, must inform. This is PIO's responsibility not yours.
Q164. Can I file same RTI to both departments to be safe? A: Technically yes but wasteful. Both will respond (you pay 3l0 each time). Better to file to primary source.
Q165. What if one department says "not with us, contact XYZ department"? A: Should be formal transfer (Section 6(3) ). If informal, you can file separately or appeal for proper transfer.

Q166. Can PMO (state chief minister's office) refuse saying "transferred to ministry"? A: Only if information is actually held elsewhere. Cannot refuse on pretext of transfer without actually transferring
Q167. What if ministry says "this is handled by state, file there"? A: If its truly state matter they must formally transfer Cannot verbally redirect without formal procedure.
Q168. Local body ( municipality ) vs state government which should I approach? A: Depends on what information. Municipal matters municipality PIO. State level state department PIO.
Q169. If information is held by both state and district office, whom do L approach? A: State level office ( SIC supervises state level) . They coordinate with district if needed.
Q170. Can I file RTI asking "which department has this information"? A: Yes, you can file meta RTI. Department should respond or direct you to correct department.
Q171. If document contains some confidential + some public info, what happens? A: Partial disclosure - public parts given, confidential parts withheld with explanation (Section 10).
Q172. Can "investigation ongoing" forever prevent disclosure? A: No, once investigation closes, information becomes accessible. 2ryear limit should be applied.
Q173. What if cabinet paper discusses corruption must it still be hidden? A: Section 8(2 ) public interest override applies Corruption disclosure overrides cabinet confidentiality
Q174. If trade secret is already publicly known, can it still be withheld? A: No, if secret is already public, exemption doesnt apply. Information already in public domain is accessible.
Q175. Can personal information be withheld if person is public figure? Aः Yes public figures less privacy protection but still some. Information must relate to public role activity. get
Q176. What if information reveals security lapse can itbe withheld? A: Tricky - security breach is public interest, but disclosing details might compound breach. Typically withheld initially.
Q177. Can draft policy be withheld forever as "draft"? A: No, once 1 2 years old, draft becomes "historical" and should be disclosed.
Q178. If government admits information would cause "embarrassment " can it refuse? A: No, embarrassment is not valid exemption. Only specific Section 8 categories apply.
Q179. Can government refuse saying "will set bad precedent"? A: precedent concerns are not valid exemptions under RTI. Each request judged on merits. No,
Q180. If both Section 8(l)(h) and 8(1) (i) apply which takes precedence? A: No precedence if any exemption applies, information can be withheld (unless Section 8(2) override applies).
Q181. What if first appeal officer says "agree with PIO, request denied"? A: You can appeal to SIC within 90 days citing reasons why officer was wrong
Q182. Can I directly go to SIC without filing first appeal? A: In some states yes (if no senior officer designated) . In Chhattisgarh, first appeal must go to designated senior officer (if any .
Q183. What if appeal officer delays beyond 45 days? A: Deemed approval information must be disclosed. You can also escalate to SIC.
Q184. Can first appeal be rejected saying "no new evidence"? A: appeal officer must review PIO decision afresh, not just accept PIO reasoning. No,
Q185. Can [ appeal PIO decision to SIC within 30 days ( before first appeal)? Aः must first appeal to senior officer first ( 30 days). Only then appeal to SIC next 90 days). No,
Q186. If first appeal officer is also biased, can I directly approach SIC? A: Tes SIC can review PIO + appeal officer decisions if bias collusion evident.
Q187. What if senior officer says "I will not hear your appeal"? A: This is violation. Appeal to SIC immediately citing refusal to hear appeal.
Q188. Can first appeal officer demand more fees? A: appeal is free. Only original 310 fee (not charged again for appeal) . NO,
Q189. What if SIC takes >90 days for decision? A: You can file High Court writ petition for delay. Or complain to Chief Commissioner
Q190. Can [ appeal High Court decision to Supreme Court? A: Tes, via Special Leave Petition to Supreme Court if High Court verdict is unreasonable.

Q191. "I suspect corruption in school tender. Can I get proof through RTI?" A: Yes. Request: tender documents bid evaluation notes, contract file. If corruption found, public interest overrides exemptions ( Section 8(2)).

Q192. "Government spent 350 lakh on consultancy but no outcome. Can I get details?" A: Yes. Request: consultancy contract, scope of work, deliverables, payment receipts. This is public interest information.
Q193. "Contractor got extension without bidding. Is this legal disclosure?" A: Yes, you can request: amendment order justification, why extension instead of rebid. Public interest applies
Q194. "Daughter got government job. Is it due to corruption? Can RTI help?" A: Request: recruitment notification, merit list, selection criteria, interview scores. Anomalies will show pattern.
Q195. "Local officials house is palace sized. How did he afford it on salary?" A: RTI can help: property records salary slips (public), assets declaration (if available). Indirect investigation tool.
Q196. "MLA allocated funds but work not visible. Can I track?" A: Yes. Request: work order, execution photographs, payment bills, inspection reports. Track every rupee
Q197. "Tender awarded to unqualified company. Can I challenge?" A: Request details through RTI. File appeal on grounds of wrongful award. Present evidence to SICIHigh Court.
Q198. "Substandard material used in construction. Where do [ get proof?" A: RTI requestः tender specifications, quality certificates inspection reports, approved samples documentation
Q199. "Government claims project complete but I don't see it. Can I verify?" A: Requestः project completion certificate, photographs, utilization certificate. Compare with ground reality
Q200. "Budget was allocated but no spending shows. Where did money A: Request: allocation details, spending ledgers, unused budget carryforward. Accounts will reveal truth. 80?"
Q201. was my child not selected for school? Can RTI help?" A: Yes. Request: merit list, selection criteria, marks of selected students, your child's scores and ranking "Why
Q202. "Teacher is unqualified. Can RTI prove this?" A: Request: teacher's appointment letter, qualifications submitted, verification done, appointment order basis.
Q203. "School collected illegal fees. How to prove?" A: Request: fee approval by government, circular on permissible fees, fee records for past years, no-objection.
Q204. "Midday meal quality is poor. Can [ get records?" A: Request: menu prescribed, bills of ingredients, vendor contracts, inspection reports, audit findings
Q205. "Principal misappropriated school funds. Wherels proof?" A: Request: budget, expense vouchers funds received vS. spent, audit report. SIC can order enquiry.
Q206. "Why were merit students denied scholarship?" A: Request: scholarship policy, eligible list, selected list, selection criteria, rejection reasons.
Q207. "School building is in ruins. no repair?" A: Request: maintenance budget allocated, repair proposals submitted, approvals, inspection reports. Why
Q208. "Textbooks have printing errors. Why printed?" A: Request: tender for textbook printing, approval process, quality checks done, error correction steps.
Q209. "Computer lab equipment bought but not installed?" A: Request: purchase order, delivery receipt, installation work order, utilization certificate.
Q210. "Why is school exam result below average?" A: Request: pass percentage, comparison with previous years, district average, reason analysis by education dept.
Q211. "Hospital lacks medicines. Is there budget?" A: Request: annual budget allocation, expenditure on medicines, inventory records, purchase orders.

chunks.question: Q20. Can [ request information in Hindi? A: Yes, you can file RTI in English, Hindi, or any official language of the area. PIO must respond in the same language or English.
Q21. How long does it take to get RTI response in Chhattisgarh? A: Standard: 30 days from receipt of application. Emergency (life liberty cases): 48 hours
Q22. If no response is received within 30 days, what happens? A: The application is "deemed refused" you can immediately appeal without waiting for formal rejection letter.
Q23. Can the 3O day deadline be extended? A: Yes if third party notification is required (Section ll ) , the deadline extends to 40 days.
Q24. What if 1 don't receive response within 30 days? A: You can file First Appeal within 30 days of the deemed refusal to a senior officer.
Q25. Will [ get response on the exact 3Oth day? A: No, deadline is "within 30 days" meaning by the end of 3Oth Response can come any up to day 30. day. day
Q26. How much is the RTI application fee in Chhattisgarh? A: 3l0 per application (onetime fee)
Q27. Are there additional charges if I want printed copies? A: Yes, copy charge is =2 per page for black & white printouts.
Q28. What if 1 want information in digital format ( CD, email)? A: You may pay cost of medium (CDIDVD) typically 310 20. Email delivery is usually free.
Q29. Are BPL persons required to pay RTI fees? A: No, completely exempt. Just provide BPL certificate copy with application
Q30. How do I pay the 3l0 fee? A: Tou can pay through:
Q31. What if I cannot afford the fee? A: File application stating economic hardship. PIO may waive fees if satisfied.
Q32. If PIO doesn t respond within 30 days, do I get free information? A: Yes! Per Section 7(6), if PIO fails to meet deadline, information is provided free of charge.
Q33. Can fees be refunded if application is rejected? A: No, application fee is non- refundable even if request is rejected.
Q34. Are there fees for First Appeal or Second Appeal? A: No appeals to SIC senior officer are free. No fee charged.
Q35. What is the maximum fee I can be charged? A: For =2 per page standard rate. Actual cost if higher No arbitrary charges allowed. copies:
Q36. What is a Public Information Officer ( PIO)? A: The designated official in each department responsible for receiving and processing RTI applications per Section 5.
Q37. How do I find the PIO of a department? A: Check the departments website name, email, phone), ask at department office, or call Suchna Aayog helpline.

Q38. Can [ file RTI with Assistant PIO instead of main PIO? A: Yes, Assistant PIO (at sub- divisional level) can accept applications. Response timeline increases by 5 days if filed with Assistant PIO.
Q39. What if PIO doesn't respond? A: Per Section 7(2), this is "deemed refusal" and you can appeal immediately
Q40. Can I ask who the PIO is? A: Tes, every department must publish PIO's name and contact details. You can request this information itself.
Q41. Can I ask for information that doesn't exist yet? A: you can only request information that already exists If it doesn't exist, PIO must reject stating reason. No,
Q42. Can I request analysis or reports not already prepared? A: you cannot ask PIO to create new reports. You can only request already existing documents. No,

Q43. Can [ request information about a specific person? A: Only if it's related to public activity or government function. Personal information unrelated to public activity is protected ( Section 8(1) (j)).
Q44. Can [ ask for copies of government contracts? A: Yes, government contracts are public information. You can request copies of contracts between government and vendors.

Q45. Can I request salary details of government employees? A: Yes, salary information of all government officers is public ( Section 4 requires this publication) . But personal details oflower staff may be protected.
Q46. Can I ask about budget allocation? A: Yes, budget allocations are public information. Every department must publish budget details (Section 4(1) (b) (xi)).
Q47. Can I request information about government meetings? A: Yes, you can request minutes of meetings, decisions taken, but not internal deliberations ( those are Cabinet papers).
Q48. Can I ask for details about government tenders? A: Yes, all tender documents, criteria, and award details are public. Sealed bids of other companies are confidential until opening.
Q49. Can I request list of beneficiaries of government scheme? A: you can request complete list of who received benefits under any government program. Yes,
Q50. Can Iask for copies of FIRs ( Police complaints)? A: Partially yes you can get details if you're a victim stakeholder Investigation details may be withheld (Section 8(1) (h)).
Q51. What information is NOT provided under RTI? A: Information falling under Sections 8&9:
Q52. Can I get information about national security? A: No, national security is exempt (Section 8(l) (a) ). But public interest can override in some cases.
Q53. Can [ request information about Cabinet discussions? A: internal Cabinet deliberations are protected ( Section 8(1) (i)). But final Cabinet decisions must be disclosed. No,
Q54. What if I want competitor information? A: Commercial confidentiality ( trade secrets) cannot be disclosed ( Section 8(a)(d) ) unless public interest is strong
Q55. Can I get medical records of patients? A: medical information is personal and private (Section 8(1) (j)) unless public health emergency. No,
Q56. Can I request sealed tender bids of other companies? A: No, sealed bids are confidential ( Section 8(1) (d)). After bid opening winners bid becomes public.
Q57. Are government employee personal details protected? A: Personal details (address, phone, family info) are protected. But official designation, salary performance is public.
Q58. Can government refuse information claiming efficiency harm? A: No, "efficiency" is not valid exemption. Only specific exemptions in Section 8 apply.
Q59. Can Ibe denied information because it's "sensitive"? A: "sensitive" alone is not valid exemption. Must fall under specific Section 8 categories. No,

Q60. What is Section 8(2) -Public Interest Override? A: Even exempt information can be disclosed if public interest in disclosure outweighs harm. Example: Corruption evidence overrides commercial confidentiality.
Q61. What is thirdrparty information? A: Information relating to another person (company, individual) provided to government in confidence.
Q62. How is third party information handled? A: PIO notifies third party within 5 gives them 10 days to object, then decides within 40 days ( not 30). days,
Q63. Can I get information about another person's RTI request? A: No, that person's information is confidential ( third party confidentiality).
Q64. Can I request tender details of competing companies? A: Preraward: NO (confidential). Post award: YES for winning company details.
Q65. What happens if third party objects to disclosure? A: PIO considers objection, applies public interest test. Objection is not automatic reason for denial.
Q66. How long does third party notification add to timeline? A: 1O additional days (third party 10 days to respond) . Total: 40 days instead of 30. gets
Q67. Can third party appeal against disclosure? A: Yes, third party can file appeal to State Information Commission against disclosure decision.
Q68. Is employee information considered "third party"? A: Partially. Public information (salary, designation ) isn't third party. Personal details (address family) are.
Q69. Can I get details about another person's contract? A: Government's side yes (contract terms, vendor details). Vendor's proprietary details may be withheld.
Q70. What if third party is a competitor bidder? A: Their sealed bid is protected. After award, winning bidder's accepted terms are public (but cost may be protected if commercial).
Q71. Can I ask for information in specific format? A: Yes, you can request printed, email, CD,or inspection. PIO should provide requested format unless resource intensive.
Q72. Can I ask to inspect records instead of getting copies? A: Tes, you have right to inspect ( Section 2(j)) this is often free and faster
Q73. Can information be provided via email? A: Tes, if applicant provides email address and PIO can digitize. Email is usually free.
Q74. What if requested format is not available? A: PIO can provide alternate format but must inform you and charge accordingly.
Q75. Can I ask for soft copies instead of printed copies? A: Yes, this reduces cost ( =2 page for vs. few rupees for CDlemail). print
Q76. Is there charge for inspection without copying? A: No, inspection is usually free. You only pay if you want copies.
Q77. Can I photograph documents during inspection? A: Personal copies during inspection are not charged (Section 7(5)).
Q78. How do 1 get information if Tm illiterate? A: PIO must provide reasonable assistance (Section 7(4 )). Can provide audio, oral, or translated version.
Q79. Can I ask for translated information? A: Yes, if you need Hindi English translation. Reasonable translation assistance must be provided.
Q80. What if document is in poor condition? A: PIO will provide best available copy. If not reproducible, must inform and may deny copy (but must allow inspection). they
Q81. Can [ request information about myself? A: Yes, you can always personal information held by government (if not restricted by other laws). get
Q82. What is "life and liberty" exception? A: Information concerning someone's lifel physical safety is urgent must be provided within 48 hours (not 30 days).
Q83. Can I request information about ongoing court case? A: Limited yes - you can request government documents filed in court. Internal investigation details may be withheld.
Q84. Can I get information during emergency? A: Yes, life liberty information 48hour deadline. Other emergencies don't have special timeline. gets
Q85. Can [ request information about police cases? A: You can request FIR details, charge sheet if you're stakeholder Investigation techniques sources are protected (Section 8(1 ) (h)).
Q86. Can I get information about election? A: Tes, election data is public. But candidate personal details and voting patterns are confidential.
Q87. Can I request information about propertylland? A: Yes, land records, property tax, ownership details are public information.
Q88. Can [ get old historical documents? A: Yes, documents 20+ years old are automatically disclosed ( Section 8(3) ) except sovereigntyllegislative privilege cabinet papers.
Q89. Can government say "file will be searched" and delay? A: No, if information exists, PIO must provide within 30 days. "File not found" is not valid excuse.
Q90. Can I request information about deceased person? A: Tes, public information about deceased officials is available. Personal details may still be protected for family

Q91. What is difference between "shall" and "may" in RTI Act? A: "Shall" = mandatory (must do). "May" = discretionary (can choose). Section 4( 2) says "shall be constant endeavor" (mandatory suo motu).
Q92. How is "reasonable time " defined for computerization? A: Not specifically defined courts interpret based on departmentis capacity. Generally 2 3 years is reasonable.
Q93. What is "disproportionate diversion of resources"? A: PIO can refuse if responding would excessively strain resources. But threshold is high must be proven.
Q94. Can PIO charge for "search and retrieval"? A: No, PIO cannot charge for finding and preparing information. Only copy costs can be charged.
Q95. Is RTI fee an application fee or information fee? A: Application fee only. You pay 310 to register request. Copy charges are separate.
Q96. What is "prescribed fee" vs "actual cost"? A: Prescribed fee is per regulation (=2 page). If actual cost is higher, PIO must justify charging more.
Q97. Can PIO refuse if applicant is serial RTI filer? A: frequency of applications doesnt matter Each application must be processed on merit. NO,
Q98. What is burden on government vs public interest? A: Section 8(2) test: Does benefit t0 public outweigh harm? Burden is not consideration -only exempt interests matter
Q99. How is "public activity" defined for privacy? A: Activities related to government functions, public interest, democratic participation. Personal hobbies medical aren t "public activity"
Q102. Can PIO demand "why" for information? A: No, Section 6(2) explicitly says reason is NOT required. Asking why is violation.
Q103. Can PIO refuse application because "not in prescribed format"? A: any format (plain letter, email, portal) is acceptable. Cannot demand specific format. NO,
Q104. What if PIO asks for more fee than prescribed? A: This is illegal. Appeal immediately citing overcharging. PIO can only charge prescribed amount.
Q106. What if multiple people request same information? A: PIO must process each separately and within 3O-day deadline for each. Cannot batch process to save time.
Q107. Can PIO delay saying "awaiting superior approval"? A: PIO has 30 Getting internal approval must happen within this time. days. NO,
Q108. Is there deadline for PIO to even register application? A: No explicit deadline but application is deemed received on receipt date ( for timeline calculation).
Q109. What if PIO transfers application to another department? A: Original timeline pauses, receiving department gets new 30 days. You should be informed within 5 Of transfer. days
Q110. Can PIO demand applicant's identity? A: No, you only need to provide contact details. Full identity personal verification cannot be demanded.
Q112. Can "official secrets" always be withheld? A: No, Section 8(2) allows disclosure if public interest outweighs official secrecy. RTI supersedes Official Secrets Act, 1923.
Q113. What is difference between "Cabinet papers" and "government decision"? A: Cabinet papers = deliberations protected) . Government decision = outcome ( must be disclosed with reasons .
Q114. Can trade secret protection last forever? A: No, after 20 years, information becomes accessible ( Section 8(3) ) unless sovereignty cabinet papers.
Q115. What if information is both personal AND public interest? A: Balance is applied. Public interest (corruption, illegality health safety) usually overrides personal privacy.
Q116. Can "preliminary assessment" stage be withheld? A: Not as blanket exemption. Investigation details can be withheld under Section 8(1) (h), not preliminary stage alone.
Q117. What is "larger public interest" test? A: Applies to Sections 8(1)(d), (e), (j). Disclosure must serve substantial public purpose, not mere curiosity.
Q118. Can live investigation details be withheld? A: Yes, Section 8(1) (h) applies. But once case is closed, information becomes accessible.
Q119. What information about ongoing litigation must be disclosed? A: Governments position papers, affidavits filed in court, factual details must be disclosed. Legal strategy may be protected.
Q120. Can "pending decision" be withheld as "draft"? A: No, pending decisions at final stage must be disclosed. Only internal draft (pre finalization) can be withheld.
Q121. What is suo motu disclosure obligation? A: Section 4(2) - Every department must proactively publish information regularly, not wait for RTI requests
Q122. What information must be published suo motu? A: Everything listed in Section 4(1)(b) 17 categories structure, budgets, contracts, beneficiaries, procedures, etc.
Q123. Does suo motu disclosure reduce RTI applications? A: Yes, and that's the goal. If information is already published, RTI process is faster
Q124. What is timeline for suo motu disclosure? A: Within 120 days of RTI Act enactment (already passed), then ongoing annual updates required.
Q125. Can department fail suo motu disclosure? A: Yes, many departments are noncompliant. You can complain to SIC about inadequate suo motu disclosure.
Q126. What if requested information is already published? A: PIO should provide reference link. Cannot charge copy fee if already publicly available.
Q127. How is suo motu disclosure monitored? A: State Information Commission prepares annual report on compliance. Citizens can also file complaints
Q128. Can departments choose what to disclose suo motu? A: Section 4(1)(b) mandates 17 specific categories. Departments cannot selectively disclose. NO,
Q129. Is department website updating considered suo motu disclosure? A: Partially yes, but Section 4 requires specific 17 items to be published within prescribed format.
Q130. What if department's website information is incomplete? A: You can file RTI for missing information, or complaint to SIC about non compliance with Section 4.
Q131. What can State Information Commission do? A: Pass binding orders on PIOs, recommend penalties (up to =25,OOO) , award compensation, initiate suo motu investigations.
Q132. Can SIC order compensation for delay ? Aः Yes, SIC can award compensation if delay caused hardship. Amount is discretionary ( =5OO 5,OOO typical).
Q133. Can SIC penalize PIO for slow response? A: Tes, can recommend penalties for repeated violations (up to 325,OO0) or disciplinary action including dismissal.
Q134. What if SIC order is not complied? A: You can file contempt petition in High Court against non compliance.
Q135. Can SIC modify PIO's decision? A: Yes, in appeal, SIC can order disclosure of previously withheld information if it disagrees with exemption claim.
Q136. Can SIC conduct suo motu investigation? A: Yes, SIC can take up suo motu cases based on media reports or public knowledge about RTI violations.
Q137. What is "larger public interest" per SIC interpretation? A: Varies by case, but generally includes corruption exposure, health safety risks constitutional violations environmental threats.
Q138. How long does SIC take to decide? A: 90 days from appeal receipt (extendable by 90 more days for complex cases).
Q139. Can SIC recommend criminal action? A: Tes, SIC can recommend police prosecution for willful violations Section 23 penalties).
Q140. Can SIC order interim relief? A: Yes, SIC can pass interim orders directing immediate disclosure while case is ongoing.
Q141. What if PIO says "file is with another department, we'll get it after 15 days"? A: PIO still has 3O day obligation. Internal delays are not excuse. You should escalate if deadline isnt met.
Q142. Can PIO extend 3O day deadline by claiming "voluminous information"? A: voluminous data is not valid reason per Section 7. PIO must manage within 30 days. No,
Q143. If 1 file RTIon 3Oth of month, when is deadline - 29th or 3Oth? A: Deadline is 30 days from receipt. If received on 3Oth, deadline is 3Oth of next month (or last day of month if shorter ).
Q144. What if received on 3lst, how is 30 days counted? A: From 3lst, counting 30 you to 3Oth of next month (or last day if shorter month). days gets
Q145. Does holiday affect the 3O day counting? A: No, 30 days means calendar including weekends holidays days,
Q146. Can PIO claim "we have to check 1O0 files for one piece of data"? A: No, compilation time is included in 3O-day deadline. Cannot demand extension for compilation.
Q1477. What if transfer happens on day 291 A: Receiving department full 30 days from transfer date, not remaining 1 gets day.
Q148. If third party objects late ( day 15 instead of day 1O), what happens? A: Depends if genuinely late (beyond 10), PIO may not consider. Or may extension if for good cause. day grant
Q149. Can multiple extensions make it 6O 90 days total? A: No, standard timeline is 30 days (or 40 with third party). Extensions only for specific circumstances.
Q150. If PIO is on leave, does timeline pause? A: No, timeline continues. Department must arrange another PIO or senior officer to handle during leave.
Q151. Can I demand PIO to "verify" if information exists? A: you describe what you want. PIO searches. If doesnt exist, PIO says SO with reasons. No,
Q152. Can I ask PIO to "create analysis" of existing data? A: you cannot ask for analysis. Tou can only request existing reports documents. No,
Q153. What if information exists but in unorganized form? A: PIO still must provide organized response within 30 days. Cannot claim "too scattered "
Q154. Can I ask for "all communications" between two people? A: Too vague. You must specify: emails, letters, meetings or which specific period project.
Q155. If data is partly digital and partly paper, can cost be charged for compilation? A: compilation and search is free. Only copy cost ( =2l page) can be charged. No,
Q156. Can I ask for information from before RTI Act came ( pre zOOS)? A: Yes, historical records are accessible. After 20 years ( 2025 for pre zoO5) , automatically accessible.
Q1577. What if record is damaged and partially illegible? A: PIO must provide available legible portions and inform about damage.
Q158. Can [ ask "what information does PIO have about X subject"? A: Too vague. You must be specific documents, reports, correspondence, etc.
Q159. If computer system has partial data for period, must full period be searched? Aः Yes, PIO must search all systems ( digital and paper). Cannot give partial just because some data is missing
Q160. Can [ ask "provide proof that decision was made transparently"? A: Too vague. Ask specifically: "minutes of meeting " "file noting " "approval email," etc.
Q161. 1 don't know which department has information can [ ask multiple? A: Better to file to likely department. If wrong, they transfer (5 days). Alternatively, file to Chief Secretary who can route.
Q162. If information is jointly held by 2 departments, where do [ file? A: File to primary coordinating department. They coordinate with other department within their 30day period.
Q163. What if PIO doesnt know whether they have information? A: PIO must search their records. If still not found, must inform. This is PIO's responsibility not yours.
Q164. Can I file same RTI to both departments to be safe? A: Technically yes but wasteful. Both will respond (you pay 3l0 each time). Better to file to primary source.
Q165. What if one department says "not with us, contact XYZ department"? A: Should be formal transfer (Section 6(3) ). If informal, you can file separately or appeal for proper transfer.

Q166. Can PMO (state chief minister's office) refuse saying "transferred to ministry"? A: Only if information is actually held elsewhere. Cannot refuse on pretext of transfer without actually transferring
Q167. What if ministry says "this is handled by state, file there"? A: If its truly state matter they must formally transfer Cannot verbally redirect without formal procedure.
Q168. Local body ( municipality ) vs state government which should I approach? A: Depends on what information. Municipal matters municipality PIO. State level state department PIO.
Q169. If information is held by both state and district office, whom do L approach? A: State level office ( SIC supervises state level) . They coordinate with district if needed.
Q170. Can I file RTI asking "which department has this information"? A: Yes, you can file meta RTI. Department should respond or direct you to correct department.
Q171. If document contains some confidential + some public info, what happens? A: Partial disclosure - public parts given, confidential parts withheld with explanation (Section 10).
Q172. Can "investigation ongoing" forever prevent disclosure? A: No, once investigation closes, information becomes accessible. 2ryear limit should be applied.
Q173. What if cabinet paper discusses corruption must it still be hidden? A: Section 8(2 ) public interest override applies Corruption disclosure overrides cabinet confidentiality
Q174. If trade secret is already publicly known, can it still be withheld? A: No, if secret is already public, exemption doesnt apply. Information already in public domain is accessible.
Q175. Can personal information be withheld if person is public figure? Aः Yes public figures less privacy protection but still some. Information must relate to public role activity. get
Q176. What if information reveals security lapse can itbe withheld? A: Tricky - security breach is public interest, but disclosing details might compound breach. Typically withheld initially.
Q177. Can draft policy be withheld forever as "draft"? A: No, once 1 2 years old, draft becomes "historical" and should be disclosed.
Q178. If government admits information would cause "embarrassment " can it refuse? A: No, embarrassment is not valid exemption. Only specific Section 8 categories apply.
Q179. Can government refuse saying "will set bad precedent"? A: precedent concerns are not valid exemptions under RTI. Each request judged on merits. No,
Q180. If both Section 8(l)(h) and 8(1) (i) apply which takes precedence? A: No precedence if any exemption applies, information can be withheld (unless Section 8(2) override applies).
Q181. What if first appeal officer says "agree with PIO, request denied"? A: You can appeal to SIC within 90 days citing reasons why officer was wrong
Q182. Can I directly go to SIC without filing first appeal? A: In some states yes (if no senior officer designated) . In Chhattisgarh, first appeal must go to designated senior officer (if any .
Q183. What if appeal officer delays beyond 45 days? A: Deemed approval information must be disclosed. You can also escalate to SIC.
Q184. Can first appeal be rejected saying "no new evidence"? A: appeal officer must review PIO decision afresh, not just accept PIO reasoning. No,
Q185. Can [ appeal PIO decision to SIC within 30 days ( before first appeal)? Aः must first appeal to senior officer first ( 30 days). Only then appeal to SIC next 90 days). No,
Q186. If first appeal officer is also biased, can I directly approach SIC? A: Tes SIC can review PIO + appeal officer decisions if bias collusion evident.
Q187. What if senior officer says "I will not hear your appeal"? A: This is violation. Appeal to SIC immediately citing refusal to hear appeal.
Q188. Can first appeal officer demand more fees? A: appeal is free. Only original 310 fee (not charged again for appeal) . NO,
Q189. What if SIC takes >90 days for decision? A: You can file High Court writ petition for delay. Or complain to Chief Commissioner
Q190. Can [ appeal High Court decision to Supreme Court? A: Tes, via Special Leave Petition to Supreme Court if High Court verdict is unreasonable.

Q191. "I suspect corruption in school tender. Can I get proof through RTI?" A: Yes. Request: tender documents bid evaluation notes, contract file. If corruption found, public interest overrides exemptions ( Section 8(2)).

Q192. "Government spent 350 lakh on consultancy but no outcome. Can I get details?" A: Yes. Request: consultancy contract, scope of work, deliverables, payment receipts. This is public interest information.
Q193. "Contractor got extension without bidding. Is this legal disclosure?" A: Yes, you can request: amendment order justification, why extension instead of rebid. Public interest applies
Q194. "Daughter got government job. Is it due to corruption? Can RTI help?" A: Request: recruitment notification, merit list, selection criteria, interview scores. Anomalies will show pattern.
Q195. "Local officials house is palace sized. How did he afford it on salary?" A: RTI can help: property records salary slips (public), assets declaration (if available). Indirect investigation tool.
Q196. "MLA allocated funds but work not visible. Can I track?" A: Yes. Request: work order, execution photographs, payment bills, inspection reports. Track every rupee
Q197. "Tender awarded to unqualified company. Can I challenge?" A: Request details through RTI. File appeal on grounds of wrongful award. Present evidence to SICIHigh Court.
Q198. "Substandard material used in construction. Where do [ get proof?" A: RTI requestः tender specifications, quality certificates inspection reports, approved samples documentation
Q199. "Government claims project complete but I don't see it. Can I verify?" A: Requestः project completion certificate, photographs, utilization certificate. Compare with ground reality
Q200. "Budget was allocated but no spending shows. Where did money A: Request: allocation details, spending ledgers, unused budget carryforward. Accounts will reveal truth. 80?"
Q201. was my child not selected for school? Can RTI help?" A: Yes. Request: merit list, selection criteria, marks of selected students, your child's scores and ranking "Why
Q202. "Teacher is unqualified. Can RTI prove this?" A: Request: teacher's appointment letter, qualifications submitted, verification done, appointment order basis.
Q203. "School collected illegal fees. How to prove?" A: Request: fee approval by government, circular on permissible fees, fee records for past years, no-objection.
Q204. "Midday meal quality is poor. Can [ get records?" A: Request: menu prescribed, bills of ingredients, vendor contracts, inspection reports, audit findings
Q205. "Principal misappropriated school funds. Wherels proof?" A: Request: budget, expense vouchers funds received vS. spent, audit report. SIC can order enquiry.
Q206. "Why were merit students denied scholarship?" A: Request: scholarship policy, eligible list, selected list, selection criteria, rejection reasons.
Q207. "School building is in ruins. no repair?" A: Request: maintenance budget allocated, repair proposals submitted, approvals, inspection reports. Why
Q208. "Textbooks have printing errors. Why printed?" A: Request: tender for textbook printing, approval process, quality checks done, error correction steps.
Q209. "Computer lab equipment bought but not installed?" A: Request: purchase order, delivery receipt, installation work order, utilization certificate.
Q210. "Why is school exam result below average?" A: Request: pass percentage, comparison with previous years, district average, reason analysis by education dept.
Q211. "Hospital lacks medicines. Is there budget?" A: Request: annual budget allocation, expenditure on medicines, inventory records, purchase orders.
Q212. "Doctor is unqualified. Can ] verify credentials?" A: Request: doctor's appointment letter qualifications submitted, verification report, recognition certificates.
Q213. "Hospital denied me treatment. Is this right?" A: Request: hospital admission policy, eligibility criteria, fee structure, complaint procedure, action taken.
Q214. "Paramedic asked bribe. Can T lodge complaint?" A: Request: complaint procedure, previous complaints against him, disciplinary action taken. Also file FIR.
Q215. "Vaccination camp not reaching villages. Why?" A: Request: immunization policy, camp schedule, resource allocation, coverage data, challenges faced.
Q216. "Drugs seized at hospital. How did they enter?" A: Request: drug procurement policy, supplier verification, batch testing storage security, audit reports
Q217. "Hospital is insanitary. What's inspection status?" A: Request: sanitation audit reports, compliance status, penalties if any corrective action plan.
